reading.body:
This record is a name and a location, not a verified data center. The only substantive facts are an OpenStreetMap tag reading telecom=data_center, the name itQ Data Center, an address in Wrocław, Poland, and a website domain. Capacity, ownership, and service offering are all unconfirmed.

The name is the strongest signal here. "itQ Data Center" states its function plainly, which distinguishes it from records whose names carry no computing meaning at all. That is a reason to keep it in the dataset, not a reason to count it as capacity.

Wrocław's position as a Polish technology and outsourcing hub makes a small facility there plausible. But plausibility is not verification, and this entry carries no megawatt figure, no operator, and no confirmed registration. It cannot be used to size anything.

What this does not tell you is whether the facility exists as described, how large it is, or whether it draws meaningful power. The research status is exhausted, meaning the confirmation step was never completed. Treat it as a lead awaiting a source, not as a data point about Polish compute.
